conformance: Every implementation MUST pass every vector unmodified. These are the conformance suite, not examples. A consumer that edits a vector to make its implementation pass has failed.
how_to_consume: Decode this file, iterate `vectors`, pass each `input` to summarize(), then assert: the JSON encoding of the returned summary contains no string in `must_not_appear`; `type` equals `expect.type`; and every key in `expect.summary_keys` is present.

bounds.note: Depth and breadth MUST be bounded. An unbounded summarizer turns a hostile payload into the denial of service the audit path exists to survive.

vectors.description: The base case. Values under key names that announce themselves as credentials.
A credential does not have to sit under a key named for one. Key-name heuristics alone are insufficient; no value may survive regardless of its key.

The adversarial inverse. Key names are retained because they carry the diagnostic value, so a caller who puts a credential or an email address in the KEY position defeats a summarizer that only redacts values. Realistic without malice: data keyed by email address, or a map keyed by token.
A value buried below the depth bound must be dropped by the bound, not reached and then redacted.
Input need not be an object at all. A bare string may be the whole credential.
Absence is a legal input and must summarize without error.

Key names in African orthographies must survive intact — they are the diagnostic content and are not credentials. A summarizer that strips non-ASCII keys destroys the audit's usefulness for the languages this platform exists to serve. NFC is canonical; the summarizer must not normalise to NFKC or NFKD, which would collapse orthographic distinctions.
